items.title: Real-Time Distributional Regime Monitoring: Online Wasserstein Detection of Market Stress
items.abstract: <jats:p>This paper develops a real-time market-stress monitor based on the geometry of rolling empirical return distributions. A strictly prior-information W1 score compares each current distribution with recursively updated low-and high-stress barycenters; thresholds are calibrated before 2007 and then frozen. Across four equity indices from 2000 through June 2026, raw DRP remains strongly scale-linked, while shapeonly DRP is much less correlated with realized volatility. In an extended seven-episode evaluation, raw DRP detects 21 of 28 market-event cases, compared with 15 for 22-day realized volatility, 14 for EWMA(0.94), and 13 for a pre-2007 fixed-parameter GARCH(1,1), while mean off-window alarm shares remain similar at 3.1%-3.5%. The paired detection advantage does not survive Holm correction, so it is interpreted as systematic but not decisive. Controlled experiments show why the distinction matters: realized volatility identifies scale shifts but is near chance for a variance-matched shape shift, whereas raw and shape-only DRP attain AUCs of 0.84 and 0.85. items.title: Cross-Asset Market Regime Detection Using Hidden Markov Models: A Framework for Real-Time Regime-Aware Risk Management
items.abstract:
<jats:p><p>Standard quantitative risk models assume financial returns follow a normal distribution with constant volatility. This paper demonstrates empirically that this assumption fails during regime shifts, producing an 11.58 percentage point underestimation of annual tail risk for S&amp;P 500 returns spanning the 2020 COVID crisis and 2022 Federal Reserve rate shock (January 2020 – December 2024).</p>
<p>We implement a cross-asset Gaussian Hidden Markov Model (HMM) — the Kroniq Regime Radar — using nine features across five asset classes: SPY, VIX, TLT, GLD, and ICE BofA US High Yield credit spreads (FRED: BAMLH0A0HYM2). A rigorous BIC model selection sweep across K=3 through K=9, with 5 independent random seeds per K and minimum state-size stability validation, confirms K=5 as the optimal and production-ready state count. Models at K=6, K=7, and K=8 produce unstable micro-states (as few as 9 days), inconsistent with reliable live regime routing.</p>

items.title: Non-parametric online market regime detection and regime clustering for multidimensional and path-dependent data structures
items.abstract: <jats:p>In this work we present a non-parametric online market regime detection method for multidimensional data structures using a path-wise two-sample test derived from a maximum mean discrepancy-based similarity metric on path space that uses rough path signatures as a feature map. The latter similarity metric has been developed and applied as a discriminator in recent generative models for small data environments, and has been optimised here to the setting where the size of new incoming data is particularly small, for faster reactivity. <br>        <br>On the same principles, we also present a path-wise method for regime clustering which extends our previous work.
